source_lines.source_with_note_markers: Sōðlice, mid-ðȳ-ðe ðæs cyninges dohtor geseah ðæt Apol-
lonius on eallum gōdum cræftum swā wel wæs getogen,[10]
ðā gefēoll hiere mōd on his lufe. Ðā, æfter ðæs bēorscipes
geęndunge, cwæð ðæt mǣden tō ðǣm cyninge: “Lēofa[11]
fæder, ðū līefdest mē, lȳtle[1] ǣr,[1] ðæt[2] ic[2] mōste[2] giefan
Apollonio swā-hwæt-swā ic wolde of ðīnum goldhorde.”
Arcestrates se cyning cwæð tō hiere: “Gief him swā-
hwæt-swā ðū wille.[3]” Hēo ðā swīðe blīðe ūtēode,[4] and
cwæð: “Lārēow[5] Apolloni, ic giefe ðē, be mīnes fæder
lēafe, twā hund punda[6] goldes,[7] and fēower hund punda[6]
gewihte[8] seolfres,[7] and ðone mǣstan dǣl dēorwurðes[9]
rēafes, and twēntig ðēowa[10] manna.[10]” And hēo ðā ðus
cwæð tō ðǣm ðēowum mannum: “Berað ðās ðing mid
ēow, ðe ic behēt Apollonio mīnum lārēowe, and lęcgeað
innan būre[11] beforan mīnum frēondum.” Ðis wearð ðā
ðus gedōn, æfter ðǣre cwēne hǣse[12]; and ealle ðā męnn
hiere giefa hęredon ðe[13] hīe gesāwon. Ðā sōðlice geęnd-
ode se gebēorscipe, and ðā męnn ealle ārison,[14] and
grētton ðone cyning and ðā cwēne, and bǣdon hīe
gesunde bēon,[15] and hām gewęndon. Ēac swilce Apol-
lonius cwæð: “Ðū gōda cyning, and earmra[16] gemiltsiend,
and ðū cwēn, lāre[16] lufiend, bēon gē gesunde.[17]” Hē
beseah ēac tō ðǣm ðēowum mannum, ðe ðæt mǣden him
forgiefen hæfde,[18] and him cwæð tō: “Nimað ðās ðing mid
ēow, ðe mē sēo cwēn forgeaf, and gān[1] wē sēcean ūre
giesthūs, ðæt wē mægen ūs[2] geręstan.”

source_span.learner_text: Sōðlice, mid-ðȳ-ðe ðæs cyninges dohtor geseah ðæt Apollonius on eallum gōdum cræftum swā wel wæs getogen, ðā gefēoll hiere mōd on his lufe. Ðā, æfter ðæs bēorscipes geęndunge, cwæð ðæt mǣden tō ðǣm cyninge: “Lēofa fæder, ðū līefdest mē, lȳtle ǣr, ðæt ic mōste giefan Apollonio swā-hwæt-swā ic wolde of ðīnum goldhorde.” Arcestrates se cyning cwæð tō hiere: “Gief him swā-hwæt-swā ðū wille.” Hēo ðā swīðe blīðe ūtēode, and cwæð: “Lārēow Apolloni, ic giefe ðē, be mīnes fæder lēafe, twā hund punda goldes, and fēower hund punda gewihte seolfres, and ðone mǣstan dǣl dēorwurðes rēafes, and twēntig ðēowa manna.” And hēo ðā ðus cwæð tō ðǣm ðēowum mannum: “Berað ðās ðing mid ēow, ðe ic behēt Apollonio mīnum lārēowe, and lęcgeað innan būre beforan mīnum frēondum.” Ðis wearð ðā ðus gedōn, æfter ðǣre cwēne hǣse; and ealle ðā męnn hiere giefa hęredon ðe hīe gesāwon. Ðā sōðlice geęndode se gebēorscipe, and ðā męnn ealle ārison, and grētton ðone cyning and ðā cwēne, and bǣdon hīe gesunde bēon, and hām gewęndon. Ēac swilce Apollonius cwæð: “Ðū gōda cyning, and earmra gemiltsiend, and ðū cwēn, lāre lufiend, bēon gē gesunde.” Hē beseah ēac tō ðǣm ðēowum mannum, ðe ðæt mǣden him forgiefen hæfde, and him cwæð tō: “Nimað ðās ðing mid ēow, ðe mē sēo cwēn forgeaf, and gān wē sēcean ūre giesthūs, ðæt wē mægen ūs geręstan.”

local_support.phrase: ealle ðā męnn hiere giefa hęredon ðe hīe gesāwon
local_support.help_text: All the men who saw them praised her gifts. The relative ðe is subject and reaches back to męnn; hīe is the accusative plural gifts. The relative clause is separated from its antecedent. Supply these reference links explicitly.
Wished them to be well: hīe refers to the king and princess and is the accusative actor of bēon; gesunde is accusative plural predicate. The complete construction is supplied.

May you be well: gē is nominative plural and gesunde nominative plural predicate. This is a direct wish with a plural subjunctive, distinct from the preceding accusative-infinitive construction despite identical gesunde.

Pitier of the poor / lover of learning. Supply both agent nouns and their object genitives. These phrases address the king and princess respectively; historical or Latin parallels in the original notes are explained in English.

local_support.help_text: The enslaved men whom the girl had given to him. Relative ðe is accusative plural; mǣden is the subject; him is Apollonius.
Said to them: him is dative plural referring to the servants; tō follows the verb while governing him.
